title: Unity VFX Entirely by AI (6.1 Sol)
author: KorvinNasa13
selftext:
I'm currently testing a pipeline (a set of custom skills) where the goal is to feed AI any image or video and have it recreate the VFX almost 1:1 in whatever style I want.

Just showing my progress so far.

I intentionally didn't make any manual adjustments. All I used was the custom skills + a screenshot (VFX) + prompt.

comments.author: KorvinNasa13
comments.body:
**Workflow**: I use Unity CLI (with all the necessary packages installed), custom agent skills and 6.1 Sol. That's basically it. I try not to overload my setup with tools and I recently got rid of MCP entirely, along with anything else that might eat up the context window.

I build the skills partly by hand, using my own VFX as examples and giving the AI corrective guidance on how motion, anticipation and other VFX best practices should work. I also go through publicly available articles and explain what information is worth extracting and adding to the skills. A lot of it is basically tedious work, constantly correcting and refining how the AI approaches creating effects.

The ultimate goal is to get the AI to produce VFX at the level of Dota, Valorant, Overwatch or Diablo.

The thing is a lot of effects in popular games actually reuse the same techniques, shaders and tricks just in different combinations. Think of it like Lego: you have a set of building blocks and you create something unique by combining them in different ways.

The important part is teaching the AI how to approach decomposition properly and what details to pay attention to. That's why my skills are pretty comprehensive and include style-specific knowledge. Even stylized VFX can be very different. Some styles rely heavily on procedural techniques with a bit of spritesheet animation, while others focus much more on hand-drawn elements, mostly using hand-painted spritesheets played frame by frame.

Procedural effects have a pretty distinct look and there are certain patterns that make them recognizable. Once you've worked in Technical Art/VFX for a while, you can often look at an effect or shader and roughly figure out which techniques are being used and how they're combined.

That's exactly the kind of knowledge I'm trying to capture in these skills. Well, technically, I just explain everything to the AI and tell it to write it into the skills, because I'm too lazy to write all of that myself, haha.

The only thing I haven't tested yet is the exact same setup but without any skills. It'd be pretty embarrassing if the results turned out way better that way 🤣
